study_identification_part.si_4_title: Individual differences v. the average patient: mapping the heterogeneity in ADHD using normative models

dc_1_datasets_using_in_this_study.detail: The study used the Dutch cohort of the International Multicenter persistent ADHD CollaboraTion (IMpACT). Data were collected at a single site (Radboud University Medical Center, Nijmegen, The Netherlands) using a single 1.5T Siemens Magnetom Avanto scanner. Although IMpACT is a multicenter initiative, only the Dutch node was used in this study, making it effectively a single-site dataset.
dc_1_datasets_using_in_this_study.supporting_text: "We selected adult participants with persistent ADHD and healthy individuals from the Dutch cohort of the International Multicenter persistent ADHD CollaboraTion (IMpACT; Hoogman et al., 2011; Mostert et al., 2015), based on data availability for structural MRI images."

dc_2_purpose_of_each_dataset.detail: The healthy control subset (N=146) of the Dutch IMpACT cohort was used to estimate the normative model via 10-fold cross-validation. The ADHD subset (N=153) was used for out-of-sample prediction to map individual deviations from the normative model.
dc_2_purpose_of_each_dataset.supporting_text: "The normative range for this model in healthy individuals was estimated using 10-fold crossvalidation, then we applied the model trained on all healthy individuals to participants with ADHD." ... "We implemented this framework using 10-fold cross-validation for healthy individuals and out-of-sample validation for individuals with ADHD."
dc_2_purpose_of_each_dataset.location: Wolfers2020.pdf.md: Methods / Normative modeling, L107; S0033291719000084sup001.docx.md: Supplemental Methods / Normative modelling, L11

model-1.model-name: gray and white matter normative model (GPR)

dc_3_number_of_healthy_control_of_each_n.detail: A single normative model was built using Gaussian process regression to predict regional gray and white matter volumes from age and sex. The model was estimated on 146 healthy controls using 10-fold cross-validation. Because 10-fold CV was used, approximately 131 subjects were used for training and 15 for testing in each fold, but exact per-fold splits are not reported.
dc_3_number_of_healthy_control_of_each_n.supporting_text: "We included 153 adults with ADHD and 146 healthy adults." ... "The normative range for this model in healthy individuals was estimated using 10-fold crossvalidation, then we applied the model trained on all healthy individuals to participants with ADHD."
dc_3_number_of_healthy_control_of_each_n.location: Wolfers2020.pdf.md: Results / Participants, L124-125; Methods / Normative modeling, L107

dc_4_age_info_of_each_normative_nodel.detail: The mean age and SD are reported for the 146 healthy controls (overall-phase) in Table 1. Per-fold train-phase statistics are not reported. The paper mentions gray matter decreases 'from age 20 to 70 years' in the normative model characterization, but this describes model behavior, not exact participant age range. The supplementary Figure S1 shows age distributions but exact min/max values are not numerically stated.
dc_4_age_info_of_each_normative_nodel.supporting_text: "Age (years) (mean ± std) 35.43 ± 12.01" ... "The average age of participants was 35 years in both groups with an age distribution that was very similar (online Supplementary Fig. S1)."
dc_4_age_info_of_each_normative_nodel.location: Wolfers2020.pdf.md: Table 1, L64; Results / Participants, L125

dc_5_sex_info_of_each_normative_nodel.detail: Table 1 reports that 43.8% of healthy individuals were male. From total N=146: male_n = round(146 × 0.438) = 64, female_n = 146 - 64 = 82, female_pct = 82/146 = 56.2%. Per-fold train-phase sex breakdowns are not reported. Sex was used as a covariate in the normative model.
dc_5_sex_info_of_each_normative_nodel.supporting_text: "Total (N) 146" ... "Males (%) 43.8%" ... "About the same proportion of individuals in both groups were male (43.8% first and 41.2% second group, respectively)."
